prose:
`run_code` executes one async JavaScript function body with top-level `await` and `return`. Orchestrate multi-step work in a single call instead of one call at a time: run independent calls concurrently with `Promise.all`, chain dependent steps with `await`, branch or nest on intermediate results, and use loops to batch or filter work. You MUST end with `return` for the data or tool results you need—return result objects directly (single result, `Promise.all` array, or summary object) for full output and metadata, or return filtered/sliced summaries; the host automatically formats returned objects, tables, and multiline strings without JSON-escaping. Only media handles (`media: [{ __litecode_media, kind, mime_type }]`) included in your `return` value are attached as multimodal outputs; unreturned media stays discarded.

Call tools as `tools.<name>(args)` (or `tools.<suite>.<member>(args)` for custom suites). A no-argument tool takes no argument; every other tool takes one object matching its declared input schema. Each call returns a promise that resolves to its declared data or rejects with an ordinary JavaScript `Error`; `try`/`catch` and `Promise.allSettled` handle rejections, and a rejected tool error carries `code`, `message`, and optional `details`. For strings containing backslashes or quotes (such as regex edits), use `String.raw` or template literals — but avoid `String.raw` or bare template literals if the embedded text itself contains backticks (`` ` ``) or `${...}` (e.g. Python docstrings, Markdown, or shell scripts), since `` ` `` cannot be backslash-escaped in `String.raw` and `${...}` is still evaluated; use regular quoted strings or concatenation instead. The declarations below are the source of truth for tool paths, argument shapes, and result fields.

`fs` is a synchronous, read-only, workspace-relative probe (`ls`/`stat` throw `Error` on missing or out-of-workspace paths). `libs` are pure-JS helpers. Both are declared below. No direct network, process, module access, or timers (`setTimeout`/`setInterval`) exist; side effects and external IO go through the bound tools.

Unknown tool bindings, output-contract violations, cancellation, the 600000 ms active JS execution cap (paused while tool calls run, subject to a 1800000 ms hard wall-clock cap per `run_code` call), and hard limits stop the cell and cannot be caught. Non-finite numbers in a result become `null` with a warning.

When any output exceeds the display limit, it is cut to a head+tail preview with `… <N> bytes total; full output: <path>`. Every path under `.litecode/run/` holds the complete unclipped output—inspect that path with bounded reads or searches instead of re-running work.

types.Integer:
/** Whole JSON number. The host rejects fractional values. @asType integer */
type Integer = number;
types.NoArgs:
/** Empty input for tools that take no arguments. */
type NoArgs = {};
types.Path:
/** Workspace-relative path, or an absolute path when explicitly allowed. */
type Path = string;

apply_edits.doc: Apply replacements serially; matching edits stay saved on disk even if another item fails and rejects. A single edit is an array of one.

read.doc: Read lines from one file or archived session transcript.

code_search.doc: Semantic search over the workspace code index.

exec_command.doc: Start a command. Waits up to yield_time_ms; a live session_id leaves it running in the background. Poll with write_stdin for output, or leave it and wait for the background-exit reminder (exit code + output_file).

write_stdin.doc: Poll, feed, or interrupt an existing exec session. Empty chars waits until the session exits or yield_time_ms expires, returning accumulated output; on exit, exit_code is set and session_id is null.

browser_click.doc: Click one interactive element on the visible page.

browser_read.doc: Read the current visible browser page.

browser_type.doc: Type text into one input on the visible page.

diagnostics.doc: List diagnostics for one source file.

document_symbol.doc: List symbols in one source file.

find_references.doc: List references at a file position.

go_to_definition.doc: Jump to definition at a file position.

go_to_implementation.doc: Jump to implementations at a file position.

hover.doc: Fetch hover docs or type information at a file position.

memory.delete.doc: Delete entries by id from the current session's working memory.

memory.list.doc: Return the authoritative current session memory snapshot; memory survives compaction and is re-injected.

memory.upsert.doc: Add or update small, durable session memory entries.

todo.write.doc: Replace the current session task list; clearing occurs automatically when all items are completed.

plan.create.doc: Propose creating a workspace plan file (opens user approval dialog). Write the plan file, then present it and ask the user to confirm before executing.

plan.finish.doc: Clear the active plan pointer on this session when finished.

ask_user.doc: Ask the user one or more structured questions via UI cards (free-text option included by system).

knowledge.check.doc: Check workspace knowledge nodes for broken citations, duplicate keys, or invalid node headers (omit filters to check all). The checked-node and issue counts are shown in the run view, not returned here.

knowledge.create.doc: Create a new pending knowledge node markdown stub under `.litecode/knowledge/`.

knowledge.list.doc: List workspace knowledge nodes as flat summary rows (omit filters to list all); nodes use a `node` fence and `[@ key="..."]` / `[@ file="..."]` citations. The corpus root and node count are shown in the run view, not returned here.

knowledge.refs.doc: Inspect one knowledge node's markdown body, incoming/outgoing citations, and issues.

workspace.help.doc: Read workspace setup or `.litecode/{excludes,mcp,custom_tools,apps}.json` configuration guides.

workspace.status.doc: Read live runtime workspace status: active excludes, loaded MCP servers, custom tools, and Apps.

subagent.launch.doc: Launch a configured subagent child session asynchronously.

subagent.list.doc: List all descendant child sessions of this session with current status and transcript metadata.

subagent.send.doc: Queue, steer, or stop-and-send a follow-up message to a child subagent session.

subagent.stop.doc: Stop the active running turn of a child subagent session.

subagent.wait.doc: Wait for selected running subagent turns (or snapshot active children) to settle.

bot.create.doc: Create a peer/owned bot with its own session in this workspace.

bot.list.doc: List visible bots in this org scope with live session status.

bot.send.doc: Queue a message for another bot's session without waiting.
